sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Mail-Order Retail with Cash on Delivery Settlement

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Common Law for federal corporate, tax, and AML statutes within a federal state; Quebec retains a civil law subsystem, while common law governs the federal jurisdiction substantive framework.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: USMCA (Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement), in force 1 July 2020
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force for Canada 30 December 2018 (covers Vietnam and Malaysia emerging-market parties)
Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA), in force 1 October 2014
Canada-Hong Kong Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA), in force 6 September 2016
Canada-Mongolia Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA), in force 16 February 2017
Convention between Canada and China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (DTAA), in force 29 December 1986
Convention between Canada and India for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (DTAA), in force 27 December 1996

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada has no federal limited partnership statute; formation is effected under an applicable provincial Limited Partnerships Act (e.g., Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.7, ss. 2, 5-9) with federal operability under the Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.), s. 96 (partnership taxation) and the Excise Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. E-15, s. 240 (GST/HST registration).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Provincial Register of Limited Partnerships (e.g., Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery) for statutory creation; Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) Business Registration Online for CA_FED federal tax registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration / Certificate of Limited Partnership (Form 2 under the provincial Limited Partnerships Act) together with federal Business Number (BN) registration application (CRA RC1).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; partners may contribute capital in cash or in kind under the Limited Partnership Agreement. No escrow account mandated for the mail-order retail / cash-on-delivery business scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the General Partner hereby establishes the Limited Partnership and subscribes for a general partnership interest, accepting the initial Limited Partners' capital subscriptions recorded in the Partnership's capital account ledger; (2) that the registered office shall be located at the address of the registered agent in the formation jurisdiction and the registered agent is appointed for service of process; (3) that [Name] is appointed Designated Officer and [Name] is appointed Compliance Officer, each with authority to file the declaration, open settlement accounts, and engage counsel; (4) that the Partnership shall remit all registration fees and maintain statutory records.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial Companies/Limited Partnerships Registrar via NUANS name search system administered by Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)/Corporations Canada
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search to confirm the proposed limited partnership name is distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing registered names. File an online name reservation request through the provincial registry portal; submit the NUANS search report and a declaration of permitted name use.
required_dossiers: Authorization from the proposed general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, select a new name from the registry response and resubmit; or appeal to the registrar with written submissions on distinctiveness within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed legal counsel or notary in the formation province; provincial registry for eventual filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the limited partnership agreement setting out capital contributions, profit-sharing, and management rights; have the general partner and all limited partners execute the agreement; prepare the prescribed Declaration (Form 2) signed by the general partner and verified before an authorized witness.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent and registered office address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any defects in the declaration and have the general partner re-execute before filing; amend the partnership agreement if the registrar raises an inconsistency.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery — Register of Limited Partnerships
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed Form 2 declaration electronically with the provincial LP registry, pay the prescribed fee (approx. CAD $60), and obtain the Certificate of Limited Partnership. The Partnership has no board of directors; the general partner acts as the governing body.
required_dossiers: Completed Form 2 Declaration of Limited Partnership
Registered office address within the formation jurisdiction
Name of registered agent and executed consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a query, respond by filing an amended declaration within 15 business days; a refused filing may be resubmitted with corrected particulars.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a federal Business Number (BN) and register the GST/HST account where taxable supply thresholds exceed CAD $30,000. Provide the partnership's legal name, governing jurisdiction, general partner details, and primary NAICS code 454110. The LP is a pass-through entity with the general partner responsible for reporting under s. 96 of the Income Tax Act.
required_dossiers: General partner identification (passport or corporate records)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the application, correct the business description or partner identifiers and resubmit through the portal; amendment or reactivation requests are processed within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Extra-Provincial Registration and Municipal Business Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial registries in each province of operation; municipal licensing department of the physical warehouse location
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LP as an extra-provincial limited partnership in each province where it carries on business. Obtain the municipal business licence for the fulfillment warehouse and, where applicable, a vendor permit under provincial consumer protection legislation governing mail-order retail.
required_dossiers: Certificate of existence from the home registry
Warehouse lease agreement or proof of premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a province refuses extra-provincial registration, provide certified copies of the original certificate and resubmit; municipalities generally allow cure of zoning or licensing defects within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED) / provincial Ministry of Economic Development; municipal business licensing division at the warehouse location
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No mandatory federal operating licence for mail-order retail with cash-on-delivery settlement; a municipal business licence and, where applicable, a provincial consumer protection vendor registration are sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — mail-order retail with COD settlement does not constitute a Schedule 1 activity under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999; no full EIA report or registration mandated
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with municipal sewer-by-law discharge limits (e.g., pH 6-9, BOD ≤ 300 mg/L) for warehouse sanitary effluent; negligible VOC emissions from packing operations; packaging waste must be managed under applicable provincial Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification under the provincial Fire Code (e.g., Ontario Fire Code, O. Reg. 213/07) for the warehouse; structural occupancy inspection by the municipal building department; workplace health and safety clearance from the provincial occupational health authority (e.g., Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development); WHMIS and first-aid compliance where employees handle goods.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online, My Business Account portal, GST/HST NETFILE, and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for export customs reporting.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Canadian limited partnership is a 'person' under the Excise Tax Act. The foreign LP must obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) and, if making taxable supplies in Canada, register for GST/HST by filing Form RC1 'Request for Business Number' with CRA or using Business Registration Online. The application must identify the partnership, the local/agent contact for service, and all partners. Registration becomes mandatory once taxable supplies in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 in a single calendar quarter or across the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters. No minimum capital is required, and non-resident ownership is permitted; however, at least one partner must be resident or the partnership must appoint a CRA-recognized representative with a Canadian address for service of notices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible / Territorial_Scope — the LP is fiscally transparent under the Income Tax Act; income and losses flow through to partners, and non-resident partners are taxable in Canada only on Canadian-source business income attributable to the partnership's permanent establishment. For GST/HST purposes, the partnership itself is the registrant rather than the individual partners.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a U.S.-style 'check-the-box' election; the LP's pass-through classification is mandatory. For GST/HST, the partners may elect under subsection 273(1) of the Excise Tax Act that the partnership's commercial activities be treated as a designated joint venture and reported by one partner, and the partnership itself may be registered as a separate person. For income tax, the partnership may elect a non-standard fiscal period under subsection 249.1(5) of the Income Tax Act. Cross-border hybrid mismatch allocations are constrained by sections 18.4 to 18.6 of the Income Tax Act, which may deny deductions where the partner's jurisdiction treats the LP as a non-transparent entity.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of gross revenue from taxable supplies made in Canada in a single calendar quarter or in the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (small-supplier threshold)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No federal mandate exists for real-time fiscal clearance, API-linked e-invoicing, or digital stamping in Canada. The CRA requires that invoices and export records be issued and retained in an accessible format, and registrants meeting prescribed revenue thresholds must file GST/HST returns electronically through GST/HST NETFILE or compatible software. E-invoicing may be exchanged voluntarily through the Pan-Canadian Peppol network, but there is no pre-clearance tax-authority approval of individual invoices before export.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods are zero-rated when supplied and exported from Canada as soon as is reasonably possible after the supply, under a contract of sale, with the exporter retaining documentary proof that the goods were shipped by commercial carrier to a foreign address (Excise Tax Act, Schedule VI, Part V). For COD mail-order sales to an emerging-market buyer, the Canadian LP must show that title and control of tangible goods passed to the non-resident buyer before use in Canada and that the shipment left Canada through customs. Ancillary freight or insurance services directly linked to the exported goods may also be zero-rated when included in the same supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration filed through CBSA (Form B13A for legacy paper filing or the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) electronic declaration, including the Cargo Control Number)
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the goods, terms of sale, and COD amount
Bill of Lading or air waybill evidencing physical export from Canada
Carrier or freight-forwarder certificate of export / proof of delivery at the foreign destination
Destination-country customs import entry or clearance receipt
Inward Remittance Certificate or foreign-exchange/wire transfer receipt evidencing COD settlement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA treats export zero-rating as a high-risk area. If the LP fails to retain the prescribed export evidence or the goods are deemed not to have been exported, the supply is reclassified as taxable at 5% GST/HST. CRA may reassess outside the normal four-year period for negligence or fraud, assess unpaid tax plus interest, deny documentary refund claims, and impose civil penalties under the Excise Tax Act for false statements or omissions. Willful tax evasion or knowingly making false or deceptive records may result in criminal prosecution and further fines and imprisonment. Export records, including customs declarations, bills of lading, and remittance evidence, must be retained for six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BoC) with shared authority over foreign exchange and monetary policy; prudential regulation of banks by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); anti-money laundering supervision by the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC); international payments infrastructure and the Lynx system operated under Payments Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible under a free-floating exchange rate regime. The Foreign Exchange Control Act has been repealed, and the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52) imposes no restrictions on current account or capital account transactions. Dividends, distributions, and partnership allocations to non-resident limited partners are freely remittable, subject solely to Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, possibly treaty-reduced) and to transparent pass-through taxation of the LP. No prior regulatory approval is required for repatriation of profits or repayment of partner loans. The Investment Canada Act applies only to acquisitions of control of Canadian businesses above the monetary thresholds; portfolio flows and routine trade payments are unrestricted.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, repatriation timeline, or queuing mechanism for export proceeds. A Canadian Limited Partnership may hold foreign currency receivables (including COD collections from emerging-market logistics partners) in domestic foreign-currency bank accounts, offshore accounts, or corporate treasury accounts without central bank reporting, except general FINTRAC reporting obligations (e.g., large virtual currency transactions, EFT reports over C$10,000, or terrorist property reporting).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (CAD) + USD Clearing Sub-Account; eligible for Escrow Account via Wealth & Trust division
Operational Account (CAD) and Foreign Currency Account (USD)
Operational Account (CAD) with Global Transfer facility
Operational Account (CAD) and USD Concentrated Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-High, with legal constraints. Airwallex (Canada) Inc. is registered as a Money Services Business (MSB) with FINTRAC; it is not a Schedule I bank, so funds are safeguarded but not insured by CDIC. It can serve as a cross-border disbursement and local-currency collection rail for COD settlements, virtual IBANs, and vendor payments. Wise Canada Inc. (also an MSB) is viable for conversion and payout, but neither can substitute for a domestic operating bank account as the primary treasury backbone. Legal constraint: any EMI must be registered under PCMLTFA and cannot open credit facilities or issue commercial letters of credit; those require a Schedule I bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is conditionally permitted; no absolute statutory mandate for physical appearance. For a Limited Partnership with non-resident partners and unsupported e-commerce cash-flow, most Schedule I banks require (i) an initial video call with the General Partner's directors and authorized signatories, (ii) original notarized Partnership Agreement and Registration Extract (provincial or federal), (iii) in-person identity verification for the designated Chief Compliance Officer at a bank branch or Canada Post agency for high-risk accounts, and (iv) a board resolution confirming the COD business model. Pure remote opening is only possible through second-tier banks or MSB-channeled accounts, at a higher fee and lower treasury capability.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partners (foreign beneficial owners) holding disproportionate capital in the partnership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current limited partnership registration certificate; complete chain of ownership to ultimate natural persons; beneficial ownership attestation listing any partner holding 25% or more; notarized partnership agreement; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds documentation (bank statements, audited financials, tax returns); Canadian criminal record check and politically exposed person (PEP) searches for each partner; if the LP is used as an investment vehicle, a clear business plan evidencing the mail-order retail purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-on-delivery (COD) collections remitted by third-party logistics partners in emerging markets, triggering unexplained third-party payment flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master logistics services agreement (with the courier) explicitly authorizing COD collection and remittance; detailed COD settlement statements with daily transaction reconciliation; expectation letter describing annual volume, average ticket size, and receiving markets; evidence of underlying customer orders (order IDs, delivery confirmations); AML/CFT policies and risk assessment of the LP; periodic independent audit confirmation of settlement flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk geographic exposure to emerging-market jurisdictions with heightened sanctions or FATF monitoring
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written country risk rating performed by the LP; sanctions screening (OFAC, UN, Canada sanctions list) of all counterparties; transaction monitoring program with geo-IP verification of customers; evidence that no COD deliveries are made to comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions; engagement of a reputable logistics partner with its own compliance program; capital injection trail proving legitimate 4791 e-commerce operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusually high velocity and cash-equivalent deposits through the operating account without invoice-backed trade documents
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly COD settlement summaries mapped to sales orders; commercial invoices, customs declarations, and postal receipt evidence; ERP-generated tax reports; audited financial statements of the LP (or its general partner); letter from a licensed Canadian accountant confirming the bookkeeping structure; detailed org chart demonstrating segregation of duties for collections and disbursements.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from the General Partner or limited partners into the LP's Canadian operating account are executed via SWIFT MT103 (or domestic Lynx transfer for CAD) with purpose code 'EQUITY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'PARTNER LOAN'. Verification protocol includes a capital call notice, partner resolution, signed subscription agreement, and remittance slip referencing the unique capital call number. FINTRAC requires an approved EFT report for any single wire of C$10,000 or more; banks also apply standard bank secrecy act checks. No exchange control permission is needed; however, if the injection originates from a foreign jurisdiction with its own capital controls (e.g., China), the remitter must obtain its local FX approval and the Canadian bank may require a source-of-funds declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlement: (i) Primary rail – SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments (customer credit transfer) via the LP's Canadian account or Airwallex virtual accounts, with purpose code 'TRADE GOODS' / 'PURCHASE OF INVENTORY'; (ii) Documentary credit – Commercial Letter of Credit (MT700, UCP600) issued by the Schedule I bank for high-value or first-time supplier orders; (iii) Cross-border CAD/USD settlement through Payments Canada's Lynx (for high-value) and the ACSS batch system (for low-value); (iv) Local emerging-market disbursement rails via logistics partners' pooled settlement systems are permissible only when accompanied by itemized COD settlement reports and API transmission to the LP's treasury system; (v) USD-denominated supplier payments routed through CHIPS or Fedwire using the correspondent bank network of the Canadian bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC FX forwards (CAD/USD, USD/EUR, CAD/GBP) with the Schedule I bank under an ISDA/CSA master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market currencies (e.g., VND, PHP, IDR, MXN, BRL, NGN) where the local FX market is restricted, cash-settled in USD or CAD
Cross-currency swaps (CAD/USD and USD/EM currency) for balance sheet hedging of inventory purchases and COD receivables
FX vanilla options (call/put on USD/CAD and on key EM currencies) for risk reversal strategies
Exchange-traded CAD/USD futures and options on the Montreal Exchange (TMX) for transparent, collateral-efficient micro-hedges
Natural hedging via multi-currency accounts (holding USD revenue in Airwallex or Canadian foreign-currency accounts) to offset payables

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (with T5013 Summary and partner slips)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the end of the partnership fiscal year; for a calendar-year LP, by May 31 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: CRA penalty of CAD 25 per day (minimum CAD 100; maximum CAD 2,500), arbitrary assessment of partnership income, and continued non-compliance may lead to tax prosecution under the Income Tax Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (for annual filers under the GST/HST regime)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the end of the GST/HST fiscal year; calendar-year registrants due by March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty and interest under the Excise Tax Act (minimum penalty of CAD 100, plus interest at prescribed rate); repeated failure to file can result in CRA arbitrary assessment and compliance order.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Provincial Limited Partnership Annual Return / Renewal (if registered or extra-provincially registered in a province)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial corporate registry (e.g., Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery; BC Corporate Registry; Alberta Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based; generally within 60 days after each anniversary of the original LP registration in that province.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Provincial late-filing penalties (typically CAD 50–300), loss of extra-provincial good standing, administrative suspension, and possible strike-off/cancellation of the LP registration if the default exceeds 1–2 years.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register Audit and Statutory Record Verification (partnership books, register of partners, and minute book reconciliation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal/general partner; producible to CRA, provincial registry, or securities regulator on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the annual compliance sign-off following fiscal year-end; must be completed prior to T5013 filing.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain current registers may result in monetary penalties under provincial LP acts, CRA access order, and adverse legal inference in partner disputes.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic federal audit requirement for a private limited partnership solely based on revenue. An independent audit is compulsory if the LP is a reporting issuer or investment fund under Canadian securities law (National Instrument 51-102), if required by the limited partnership agreement, or if demanded by CRA under subsection 231.5(1) of the Income Tax Act because the books are inadequate.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable/issuer LPs; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) is generally permitted for private LPs. CRA requires the accounting framework used to support the T5013 allocations and true partnership income.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Federal law does not impose a dedicated annual UBO filing for LPs, but the LP must keep its register of limited/general partners current. At each fiscal year-end, reconcile all transfers of partnership interests, obtain written confirmations of ownership percentages from partners, and retain the updated register and transfer instruments for at least 7 years. For any FINTRAC-covered business line, conduct enhanced beneficial-owner verification in accordance with the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of General Partners (including directors if corporate general partner)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% federal corporate income tax rate (general/non-CCPC rate; provincial/territorial rates are additional, ranging from 0% to 16%). A Canadian Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent: the LP itself pays no federal income tax; income is allocated to partners and taxed at the partner level (corporate partner via T2, individual partner via T1, non-resident partner via Part I return or Part XIII withholding).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) small business deduction reduces the federal rate to 9% on active business income up to CA$500,000 (allocable to a qualifying corporate general partner); Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits at 35% refundable (CCPC) or 15% non-refundable (non-CCPC); Accelerated Investment Incentive and Accelerated Capital Cost Allowance on eligible digital-ecommerce and logistics assets; DTA treaty relief on distributions to non-resident partners.
